comments.text: Jersey’s a great place to live, except for a corrupt, greedy government which is slowly strangling us.

comments.author: @blueskiesatx
comments.text:
I grew up in Warren County in the 60s and 70s in an old Stone farmhouse and of course I had horses. 

I left for a very long time and ended up moving back here when I was in my 60s. It always feels like home to me.

When people come to visit, they are astonished that New Jersey isn’t all cities, and suburbs and highways and the turnpike. We have mountains, the shore, farms and horses, and the four most perfect seasons of any state in my opinion.

replies.author: @blueskiesatx

replies.author: @rmas32
replies.text: I have family in Southern California and all they ever knew of Jersey was what they’d seen on The Sopranos! Several years ago I decided to give them a Jersey reality tour. They couldn’t believe all the farms, horses, beautiful parks, etc. At one point one asked, “Are we in Pennsylvania?” We have a beautiful state. The only thing I despise are the people who run it.

comments.author: @Rickyrab
comments.text: Um, New Jersey also has suburbs....

replies.author: @Rickyrab
replies.text: There's also New Brunswick. That's NJ's other quintessential college town, oriented around Rutgers University and hospitals (and Johnson and Johnson).

replies.author: @Rickyrab
replies.text: And you left out Rust Belt cities like Camden and Newark (yeah, I know, abandoned building central, but those cities have been on the upswing in recent years).

replies.author: @Rickyrab
replies.text:
And by "suburbs" I mean both the older suburbs of the northeast - places like Cresskill and Oradell - and mid to late 20th century 'burbs like Woodbridge and East Brunswick and Willingboro. 

You're also missing old industrial company towns like Helmetta, oriented around ancient brick mills no longer manufacturing stuff. 

There's also Edison, which is both a suburb and the location of the Thomas Edison light bulb monument, and nearby Metropark, an "edge city" of large office buildings.

replies.author: @my1ernest
replies.text: I have lived in NJ for 26 years. I was born in NYC and moved here when I was 37 years old. Ever since I was a little girl I wanted to move from there. I hated being surrounded by tall skyscrapers and people crunched together walking down the streets. For many of the things that make people from all over the world dream to visit New York City, when you're born and lived there a good portion of your life it's just ho-hum seeing those famous sites that NYC is famous for. I fell in love with NJ as soon as I moved here. Whenever I need to go visit the city all I have to do is jump on a train or bus and I'm there within an hour.
